print_errors.note: In «فَإِنْ شَكَرُوا وَأَطَاعُوا أَثَبْتَهُمْ» (line 2) the print has a fatha over ث and a sukun over ب (expected أَثْبَتَهُمْ). At 5000 dpi the أ's fatha, a second separate fatha above the ث dots and a sukun hook above the ب tooth are all distinct, so it is kept as printed.
In الصلاة البرزخية (٧) the dal has a fatha and no kasra (expected سَيِّدِنا). Days 1 and 2 (pp.100, 110) have the same misprint.
The final dal of both words has a damma above and a kasra below, kept as printed (same as pp.100, 110).

notes: p121: p120 ends item ٣٥ with a full stop and has no footnotes, so p121 opens a new paragraph (item ٣٦, no '+', no (تابع)). The divine Name شَكُورُ is red (==…==). Only «الشَّاكِرُ» after «فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ» is bold, and the hadith «لَا أُحْصِي ثَنَاءً عَلَيْكَ، أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثْنَيْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ» is bold (round-sukun bold font); the « » are left outside the bold markers. «إمامِ» has a hamza under the alif with no kasra, written as printed. p122 continues the sentence «صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ / وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ» (marker 122+); «قال» is unvowelled and «عَلَيْهِم» has no sukun on the final mim, both as printed. p123 starts day 3 (## heading, then ### الصلاة البرزخية / ### صلاة التجلي). The An-Naml 6 quote closes with ﴾ on p123 and its reference «[النمل: ٦]» opens p124, so p124 has the '+' marker. «الأَعْظَمِ» on p123 has no sukun on the lam and «المُتَخَلِّقِ» on p124 has only a damma over the lam-mim (checked at 2400 dpi), but «الْأَعْظَمِ» on p124 has the sukun; all as printed. In «الْمُسْتَقِيمِ» (p124) the lam sukun and mim damma overlap; read as both. The word Allah with a printed case vowel (اللهُ on p121 and p124, اللهَ on p122) is written fully vowelled اللَّهُ / اللَّهَ per CONVENTIONS §2, as in my b28. Final ى with the automatic small alif is written plain (عَلَى، حَتَّى، صَلَّى، مَجْلَى، مُصْطَفَى، إلى، الشورى); in Quran text إِلَىٰ keeps the dagger as in the mushaf font. I took the last line of p124 «يَا اللهُ، يَا اللهُ، يَا اللهُ(٢)» as not bold, as in b28. Footnote volume/page refs are written without a space after the slash: (٤/٣٩٨)، (١٨/١٣٥)، (٤/٣٣٩)، (١٧/٣٨٠). I measured the gaps at 1600 dpi. The gap on the left of the slash is always about 20-40 px wider than on the right, and the difference is the same in all four, including (٤/٣٣٩), which clearly has no space. That is less than a word space, so I read it as the slash glyph's own spacing. The one with ٠ can look spaced at low zoom only because the ٠ dot is narrow. scripts/quran.py gives one flag: Tanzil has the waqf sign ۖ after «لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ» (14:7), but the print closes the quote right after the word with no sign (checked at 1600 dpi), so it is left out. All other Quran spans (Saba 13, Anbiya 107, Naml 6, Shura 52) match Tanzil. validate.py: OK, no warnings.
